explanation: The deterministic pipeline found no supported physical failure events (n_physical_events=0) and reports verdict failure due to incorrect final placement, not a localized drop/release. End-of-episode geometry shows one green plate inside the rack, one outside, and one with insufficient geometry (unknown), so not all expected plates are established inside. Gripper opening was measured at ~50.9s but holding is not detectable from this joint, and no rest→move→rest release was reconstructed.

factual_claims.text: Pipeline reported zero physical failure events for this window; no rest→move→rest release event was reconstructed.
Measured gripper opening at frame 1528 (50.933s) is observed, but opening alone is not a drop and holding is not detectable from this joint.
Gripper reading cannot show whether an object is held; a thin plate does not change the closed reading (0.4-0.6 measured vs commanded ~-0.2).
End-of-episode plate observations: one region=inside, one region=outside, one region=unknown; end_state_verdict=failure.
Not every expected object has an established final position: green plate 0/? established inside.
Final-state regions are 2D image-plane containment vs dish-rack footprint/eroded interior only; incorrect orientation (e.g. plate lying flat) is NOT verified by this geometry.
Window track coverage for green plates 1498-1618 (120 frames each) is present but is not a failure event.

hypotheses.text: The plate observed outside at end-of-episode may have never been placed in the rack, or may have been placed and then displaced; pipeline provides no verified physical event to distinguish.
The unknown-region plate may be partially occluded or at rack edge causing insufficient geometry for inside/outside determination.

visual_interpretations.text: F0 (49.933s) appears to show robot arm over dish rack with two green plates already in rack and one green plate on table; no gripper object clearly visible.
F1 (50.933s) corresponds to measured gripper opening; visually gripper appears open/empty above rack.
F2 (53.9s) appears to show robot holding green whisk over table, not a plate.
F3 (69.167s) end-state appears to show two plates in rack, whisk in rack, and one green plate on table outside rack, consistent with outside detection.

limitations: Gripper joint cannot indicate holding; thin plates do not change closed reading (E0).
Final-state geometry is 2D containment only; orientation failures may remain uncertain (E3).
Object ids from window video vs end-of-episode image are not assumed same physical instance.
No physical_events were verified; do not infer drops/releases from images alone.
